short: Only new mapping work (M06) is a BLSTM and a 4-way ranking, standard; direct route (M08) inherited; no silent test (M04) or listener transcription (M12), behind; identity/mood retention unmeasured.
position: The paper [@janke2017emg] changes one component, the mapping model (M06), only by adding a BLSTM and ranking four mappings, three of them the group's earlier work, on 83 evaluation utterances and single runs (Table I). Its direct route (M08) is inherited: 13 of 14 indexed prior synthesis studies mapped directly (Appendix); the design argued against, EMG recognition to text, was the majority output and had not been paired with synthesis from EMG. Two incidental components are behind on the best comparable work: no silent articulation is tested (M04), as six prior studies did, including the group's own [@toth2009synthesizing], and no listener transcription is run (M12), a minority practice (5 of 14) that no prior EMG study used. The strongest overreach is the Abstract's claim that speaker identity and mood are retained, which no experiment measures (Abstract; §VI; Table III). The label-free claim (§I) fails for the LDA-based GMM and LSTM, not the DNN (§III-A).
